Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout latency spike impacting orders (P0)

Elaine — thanks for the heads-up and really sorry for the impact. A few quick notes while the team completes triage: we have a bridge up and are treating this as a P0.

Immediate items:
- Triage lead: Kimberly Park (on the bridge).
- Short-term mitigation: we have rolled back the new batching heuristic on the model serving fleet (applied 09:22 PDT) and enabled additional autoscale headroom in the us-west region. Initial improvement seen in 95p latency within 15 minutes.
- Investigation focus: KV cache churn + new kernel selection path when sequence lengths expanded beyond expected; this combination amplified CPU-GPU cross-talk and raised token processing latency under specific workload shapes.

Proposed readout: 11:00 PDT today with Summit SREs + Redwood ENG leadership (Kimberly, Karthik). Confirming availability from our side, but please let us know any slot constraints. We will bring an initial RCA draft and mitigations.

I'll circulate an RCA + runbook by EOD and list owners for outstanding items.

— Priyom
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout latency spike impacting orders (P0) — RCA & next steps

Elaine / Samir — thank you for joining the bridge. Attached is the RCA packet (summit_rca_v1.pdf) and the mitigation runbook we executed (mitigation_runbook.xlsx). Summary below.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: A combined regression introduced in the 2028-06-23 runtime deploy changed batching thresholds in low-latency mode and a lightweight kernel-selection optimization that assumed a narrower sequence-length distribution. For Summit's checkout prompts (median sequence ~210 tokens with wide tail), those heuristics caused repeated KV cache evictions and micro-bursts of oversized batches that overloaded the token scheduler momentarily.
- Impact: Elevated tail latency (95–99.9p) and a correlated rise in 5xx responses between 08:40–10:05 PDT affecting ~12% of checkout traffic. Estimated lost conversions: ~0.7% revenue impact for affected window.
- Mitigation completed: 09:22 PDT rollback of new batching heuristic + reverted kernel-selection flag for the affected instance pool; autoscale headroom increased by ~30% in us-west. Metrics returned to baseline by 09:58 PDT.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Short-term verification (owner: Naomi Feldman) — run 48h of stress verification against Summit traffic shape and validate tail latency stability. ETA: 2028-06-26 17:00 PDT.
2) Runtime patch (owner: Karthik Iyer) — produce a robust kernel-selection fallback that preserves the optimization for common cases but avoids KV churn under heavy-tail sequences. ETA: 2028-07-03.
3) Autoscale policy tuning (owner: Kimberly Park) — adjust warm pool thresholds for dedicated customers and document thresholds in Redwood Console. ETA: 2028-06-29.
4) Postmortem & credits (owner: Priyom Das) — coordinate commercial remediation (service credit request) and executive readout. Draft credit memo to Summit procurement. ETA: 2028-06-25.

We've included raw trace excerpts in latency_trace_20280624.txt and a short verification script in the Drive link. Please call out any missing items and confirm the readout time — we have the exec slot at 15:00 PDT today if that works for Summit leadership.

Attachments: summit_rca_v1.pdf, mitigation_runbook.xlsx, latency_trace_20280624.txt

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
